messages:
deploy-bot: Starting staged rollout: service=generation-service, from=redwood/gen-v1.3.0 to=redwood/gen-v1.4.0, target=10% (ap-south), rollout_id=rl-4520, change_window=2026-03-24T02:00Z..03:00Z
release-manager: release notes live: https://go/redwood/releases/1.4.0. QA summary uploaded. Heads-up: model tweak to beam search and token-filtering.
jordan: quick check — is this the new prune-decoder branch or the latency-optimized decoder?
claire: latency-optimized decoder (fp16 with cache-compact). Perf notes in doc. Expect ~15% latency reduction.
qa-engineer: ran smoke on canned set preflight — small formatting issue on long lists: extra commas in numbered outputs. Logging ticket opened: GH-4123. Not a blocker for perf but could affect parsers.
sre-oncall: baseline SLOs: p95 < 180ms, p99 < 420ms, 5xx < 0.3%. Auto-rollout rule: if 5xx > 0.5% sustained 5m -> auto-rollback.
infra: we'll pin infra-side lb rule to route canary slice to pooled-nodes-ap-south-2.
release-manager: set expectation: we hold at 10m for 20m baseline then consider ramp to 30%.
deploy-bot: traffic shifted to 10% in ap-south. phase=running.
jordan: noticing increased generation truncation warnings. sample from logs:
```
[2026-03-24T02:04:11Z] req=xyz gen_truncation=true reason=max_len host=gen-worker-7
```
claire: interesting — we didn't change max_len. Could be new token-filter causing early EOS.
qa-engineer: also seeing a degradation in BLEU-like metric on a small eval set (~6% drop). Pushing full snapshot to the release doc.
sre-oncall: I'm seeing p99 climb to ~520ms (from 410) for ap-south-2 over last 6m. 5xx still low (0.15%).
release-manager: decision call: do we STOP, ROLLBACK, or THROTTLE? I'm leaning throttle+investigate for now. Thoughts?
jordan: throttle concurrency for canary to 4 per-worker and reduce batch-size to 2. That should ease tail.
infra: applying concurrency override and batch-size override to rollout_id=rl-4520 now.
deploy-bot: updated rollout config: overrides={concurrency:4, batch_size:2} for rl-4520.
claire: thanks — if the truncation is token-filter related we should also temporarily flip filter to permissive mode. Can we add a soft-flag for the canary?
deploy-bot: added runtime flag canary.token_filter=permissive for rollout_id=rl-4520.
qa-engineer: reran a quick set after throttle+flag: BLEU drop reduced to 2.1% and p99 down to 430ms. Improvement visible.
sre-oncall: tail still slightly elevated but trending down. keeping alerting on.
release-manager: marking this thread: THROTTLED. Hold at 10% for another 15m. If metrics are stable, ramp to 30%. If p99 > 500ms or BLEU-drop > 5% -> rollback.
claire: I'll open a follow-up to revert the token-filter change once we have a fix. Ticket GH-4124.
jordan: note — if we decide to roll forward, plan to split canary across ap-south-1/2 to validate infra variance.
infra: we prefer to keep pinned to ap-south-2 for now; cross-region introduces noise.
qa-engineer: tagging logs + sample outputs in the release doc for triage.
sre-oncall: adding k8s OOM kills and worker restart rates to the watchdash.
release-manager: OK. No "rollback" from PM. If anyone needs to stop it now, say "stop" in this thread.
claire: not seeing cause yet, prefer hold.
jordan: ack. I'll coordinate with model team to test token-filter fix in a dev slice.
infra: infra changes applied. Observability should reflect new concurrency limits in ~90s.
qa-engineer: metrics look steady so far at 02:14Z. p99 ~ 420ms, BLEU-drop 1.8%.
sre-oncall: continuing to monitor for 10m. If anything crosses, I'll trigger auto-rollback per rule.
release-manager: thanks team — next check-in 02:30Z or earlier on signal. :thumbsup:
